organizer: Turkish Philanthropy Funds (donor-advised fund established by Hikmet and Marilyn Üçok)
eligibility_verbatim: Female and a citizen of Türkiye; preference given to healthcare and special education programs at accredited universities (preference for California, USA) but 'the scope of the scholarship encompasses other disciplines as well'; minimum high school GPA 3.50, TOEFL 80+ (or IELTS 6.5+), SAT 1300+; must demonstrate financial need; application requires the admission decision letter received from a US university.
eligible_grades: High school seniors who have been admitted to a US undergraduate program
turkey_access_reasoning: Official tpfund.org page confirms eligibility requires being 'a citizen of Türkiye' with no US residency requirement -- explicitly designed for young women who completed or will complete high school in Türkiye and then move to the US for a 4-year undergraduate degree. Not a diaspora-only or already-in-the-US program, unlike most other Turkish-American organizations' scholarships found in this research pass.
international_access_notes: Funds a 4-year undergraduate degree in the United States (up to $50,000/year, renewed automatically while the student maintains a 3.50+ GPA). Preference for California institutions and health sciences/special education fields, but other disciplines are explicitly in scope.
geographic_restrictions: Applicant must be a citizen of Türkiye; funds study specifically in the United States.
current_cycle_label: Applications currently closed; next cycle opens Fall 2027 for the 2028-29 academic year
output_type: undergraduate degree from a US university

evidence.raw_excerpt: female and a citizen of Türkiye... up to $50,000 [annually, four years, renewed automatically with 3.50+ GPA]... Applications for the Üçok Family Scholarship Fund are now closed [next cycle Fall 2027 for 2028-29]... the admission decision letter received from university... 3.50+ high school GPA, TOEFL 80+ (or IELTS 6.5+), SAT 1300+... the scope of the scholarship encompasses other disciplines as well.

notes_uncertainties: Direct WebFetch of https://www.tpfund.org/theucokfamilyscholarshipfund/ (a URL surfaced by one search result) returned 404; the working official URL is https://www.tpfund.org/scholarships/ucok-family/, fetched successfully and quoted above. Gender-restricted (women only) with a strong preference (not a hard requirement) for health sciences/special education and California institutions -- product copy should present this as a strong-fit-for-some option, not universal. Next cycle is over a year away (Fall 2027) as of this research date, so not immediately actionable, but is a real, well-documented, generously-funded program worth surfacing well in advance to eligible users given the distant deadline. This is the clearest genuine match found in this research pass for 'Turkish diaspora/bilateral cultural-society scholarship that funds study abroad and is accessible to a general Turkey-based applicant' -- most other Turkish-American organizations' programs either fund the opposite direction (Americans studying in Turkey, e.g. Turkish Coalition of America) or require the applicant to already hold a secured scholarship/admission with funding before applying (e.g. American Turkish Society's Promising Turks Fund, TPF's own Changemaker Scholarship Fund), making them supplementary top-ups rather than standalone opportunities -- see s7a1w2_rejected.jsonl for those.

eligibility_verbatim: Young changemakers 'aged 11-25 years of age at the time of the event', across four categories: Educational Innovation, Environmental Regeneration, Empowering Everyone, and Creative Rejuvenation. No country restrictions found; nominations previously received from 96 countries.
eligible_grades: Roughly grades 6-12 and beyond (age-based, not grade-based)
turkey_access_reasoning: Official legacyprojectglobal.com page states no country/nationality restriction, and the program has received nominations from 96 countries globally; the format is fully online for 2026, removing travel/visa barriers to participation. Condition: the process is framed as 'nomination'-based rather than a plain open application, and the official FAQ does not explicitly confirm whether a student may nominate themselves versus needing a third party (teacher, mentor, organization) to nominate them -- the FAQ states 'We only have the names of nominees, not nominators,' which suggests the nominee/nominator distinction may not be strictly enforced in practice, but this is inference rather than direct confirmation, so capped at ELIGIBLE_WITH_CONDITIONS rather than VERIFIED_ELIGIBLE.
international_access_notes: Delivered fully online via the 'Global Youth Hub' for the 2026 edition, removing the need for travel to participate, be shortlisted, or win.
output_type: invitation to the Global Change Ambassador network (finalists)
access to the Legacy platform's support and personal-development ecosystem for all participants

evidence.raw_excerpt: The Global Youth Awards discover and celebrate young people who are creating meaningful change in the world... aged 11-25 years of age at the time of the event... Nominations open: 1st March... Submission closing date: 1st September... Every participant gains access to support, personal development and a global ecosystem of opportunity through the Legacy platform.
We only have the names of nominees, not nominators [FAQ text; self-nomination is not explicitly confirmed or denied].

notes_uncertainties: Well-established program (13th edition in 2025, per independent local-press coverage of the 2025 ceremony reporting '39 finalists from 15 countries'), run by a UK-registered charity, in the same worldwide-open teen recognition family as the already-accepted Diana Award and Global Student Prize -- do not merge/confuse with either. 2026 deadline (September 1) is very close to this research date (August 26) -- flag for the product owner that this is time-sensitive if surfaced to users this cycle. Main open question is whether self-nomination is genuinely permitted (vs. requiring a teacher/mentor/organization to nominate) -- next reviewer should email erin@legacyprojectglobal.com or check the Global Youth Hub directly to confirm before upgrading to VERIFIED.
